title: Odile and the Inheritance
premise: Wren Coldharbour, a meticulous small-town coroner, receives a retainer from a stranger named Odile to prove a murder will not occur — the predicted victim is Odile herself, and the predicted killer is Wren's estranged brother. To prevent it, Wren must reopen the drowning of their father twelve years ago, a case the town sealed as an accident and the statute of limitations is about to close forever. As Wren digs, they discover their father's will, the town's founding families, and Odile are all tangled in one inheritance scheme built on that old death. In the end, Wren proves the father was murdered by the town's beloved matriarch, saves Odile by letting the truth — not violence — be the weapon, and must decide whether loyalty to family is worth more than the truth that destroyed it.
about_author: Odile Almeida is the pen name of a former rural death investigator who spent a decade signing certificates in towns where everyone knew everyone. They write mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside close-knit communities.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Wren Coldharbour's POV. A pale, precise stranger named Odile pays Wren a year's fees in advance to prove that no murder has happened yet — hers. The predicted killer: Wren's brother Elias. Wren, who has quietly corrected three 'accidents' the police ignored, accepts out of disbelief and dread. The beat is cold unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks the cemetery cataloguing deaths, establishing the town's intimacy with its dead, and pulls the file on their father's drowning twelve years ago — the case everyone, including Elias, swore was closed. The autopsy notes don't match the water. The emotional beat: grief reopening like a scar.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Left
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias returns to town for the reading of the matriarch Vivienne Ashcombe's revised will, unaware Wren has been hired against him. Through his eyes we see his debts, his desperation, and his genuine confusion about their father's death. Beat: sympathy for the accused.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Exhumation of the father's body reveals diatoms consistent with a live drowning — but bruising on the jaw predates it. Someone held him under. Wren realizes the 'closed' case was closed by Vivienne Ashcombe, the town's benefactor who paid for everyone's funerals. Beat: the ground shifts.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile is revealed as Vivienne's disinherited granddaughter, armed with her grandmother's ledgers showing decades of payments — hush money, funeral costs, the retainer itself. She hired Wren because she predicted Elias would be framed for killing her before the statute expires and buries the truth. Beat: ally or manipulator?

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Will
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The revised will leaves everything to Odile — but only if she survives thirty days, and void if the father's death is ruled murder. Suddenly the frame on Elias makes sense: someone needs Odile dead and the case closed. Wren finds the town doctor falsified the original autopsy. Beat: paranoia spreads through a town that owes Vivienne everything.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Wren and Elias. With nine days left, Wren and Elias reconcile over their father's grave, each admitting what they suspected and never said. Elias reveals Vivienne's son — Odile's father — was present the night of the drowning. Beat: loyalty rekindled, but the clock is merciless.

chapters.title: The House on Coldharbour Hill
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Vivienne, now dying and lucid, who neither confesses nor denies but hands over the deed to the cemetery — she owns the ground every body rests in, the leverage that silenced the town. That night Odile is attacked and survives; the doctor is found dead, staged as suicide. Beat: the noose tightens.

chapters.title: Drowning in Reverse
chapters.summary: Climax, Wren's POV. The true killer — Vivienne's caretaker and illegitimate son, protecting the inheritance — lures Wren and Odile to the old boathouse where their father died. Wren survives by turning the killer's own confession into a recorded statement, then holds him at the water's edge and chooses the law over vengeance. Beat: the price of survival, paid in restraint.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, weeks later. The father's death is ruled homicide; the will's murder clause voids, and Odile, now wealthy, funds the exhumations of every 'accident' Wren ever doubted. Elias leaves town forgiven; Wren stays, keeper of the graves. Final beat: the true inheritance is not money but the truth, and the cost of carrying it.
